# dsh-customisations

One profile plugin that carries small, independent DeepSeek Harness fixes.
Instead of a package per

workaround, every fix is a module with a stable id, so
the bundle stays one install, one patch row,

and one health line while the fix
list grows.

Today the bundle contains one fix: **currency-guard**, which stops DSH's
single-dollar inline math f
rom swallowing prose.

## Fixes
### `currency-guard`

DSH's chat markdown enables micromark inline math with `singleDollarTextMath`
and **no currency guar

d**. A reply that writes money with `$` therefore pairs
the first two dollars in a paragraph into on

that writes money with `$` therefore pairs
the first two dollars in a paragraph into one KaTeX span:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

...renders as one math run: spaces collapse (`228.21andneverreplaced`), prose
turns italic, the clos

ing `**` prints as `∗ ∗`, and a `&` inside the span (as in
`P&L`) makes KaTeX fail and print the who

le span source in `#cc0000` red.
GenUI's own inline renderer is not involved: its single-`$` rule re

jects a
closing `$` followed by a digit, so the same text renders correctly there.
### The general rule

A single `$` pair is inline math, so **any two unescaped `$` outside code in one
Markdown text block

become one math span** — the first and second pair, the third
and fourth, and so on. Currency is ju

st the most common way to produce them.
Inside that span:

- whitespace collapses and letters turn italic;
- `**` / `==` stop being Markdown and print literall

e in `#cc0000` red (`P&L` is enough);
- the span can cross sentences and blank lines inside the bloc

k;
- an odd trailing `$` has no partner and stays literal.
So the fix has to decide, per dollar pair, whether it is math or prose.
### The fix

It wraps the documented `llm/stream` waterfall (the same seam `dsh-llm-retry`,
`dsh-llm-replay`, and
`dsh-session-checkpoint-policy` use) and runs two passes:

1. **Streaming deltas** — escape a currency-shaped `$` the moment it arrives, so
the live view is co

rrect while the reply streams.
2. **Terminal `block-end`** — the adapter's full block text is what
`

BlockAssembler` treats as authoritative, so it gets the general pass: pair
every unescaped `$` outsi

de fenced and inline code, and escape both ends of a
pair whose body reads as prose (longer than 80

characters, contains `**`/`==`,
a blank line, a bare `&`, or an ordinary word of three or more lette

rs
outside a command argument). Real math is left alone.
Markdown renders `\$` as a literal `$`, so the visible reply is unchanged.

- Currency is always escaped, paired or not: `$1,234`, `$5.`, `($5)`, `$97,600,`,
`$5k`, `$1.2M`, `$

0.5%`.
- Prose pairs are escaped: `$quick brown fox$`, `−$5,833 … −$4,119`.
- Real math is preserved

: `$x^2$`, `$2\pi r$`, `$E = mc^2$`, `$5$`.
- Fenced code blocks and inline code are untouched, incl

uding shell `$1`.
- A trailing `$`/amount or backtick run is held across deltas, so a token split
be

tween chunks is still decided correctly.
- Plain-text consumers such as session titles (`purpose: "s

ession-title"`) are
skipped, where a stored `\$` would show a backslash.
- Fail-open: a transform er
ror passes the original chunk through.

Limits: only new assistant text is guarded (history keeps its `$`), and
user-authored text never pas

ses through `llm/stream`. A non-currency pair can
flash as math in the live view until the block set

tles, because only the
terminal pass has the whole block to pair. When DSH's tokenizer grows a curre

ncy
guard, remove this fix.

## Adding a fix

1. Add `lib/fixes/<id>.js` exporting `id` and `apply(ctx, config)`; install the
seam it needs there

(waterfall listener, slot, instruction, ...).
2. List it in `lib/fixes/index.js`.
3. Extend `inject`

in `lib/index.js` if the fix consumes another service.
4. Add a test that the fix installs and that
it is skipped by `disabled`.

Keep each fix fail-open and idempotent: the bundle is installed once per
profile, and one broken fix
must not take the others down.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The suite covers the reported reply end-to-end: the unguarded text parses into
three `inlineMath` no

des (one containing `P&L`), the guarded text parses into
none, and the only change to the text is a

backslash before each currency
dollar.
